selectionSummary: Continues the three events selected in the existing daily news task, after fresh source inspection. Selection weighs international security, energy exposure and long-term climate consequences; it is an editorial choice. Two inaccessible original links were replaced with accessible AP syndications, Sputnik with TASS, and the climate reference with UNEP’s explanatory news story. This edition covers the completed Paris calendar day, not the following day.

snapshot.summary: Iranian shipping claims, continued strikes in the Russia–Ukraine war, and a new climate assessment put energy and international cooperation under scrutiny. Military assertions remained disputed; climate pathways remained conditional.
connections: Editorial interpretation: energy security links the maritime crisis, attacks on infrastructure and climate policy, although the stories operate on different timescales.
uncertainties: The scale of military damage and prospects for de-escalation remained uncertain.
Emissions projections depended on future policy choices and technological feasibility.

stories.title: Iran claims seven vessels were hit near Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran’s navy announced attacks and mine incidents involving seven vessels, alongside a warning to US bases. The incidents were not independently established in the selected reporting.
stories.whyItMatters: The waterway links regional conflict with international energy transport and shipping risk.
stories.selectionRationale: Potential cross-border energy disruption and military escalation justify inclusion.
stories.evidenceNote: Separate newsrooms largely describe the same IRGC statement. Corroboration establishes that the statement was made, not that all claimed incidents occurred.

stories.title: Climate assessment shifts attention to limiting overshoot
stories.summary: Coverage of UNEP’s new assessment examined pathways beyond 1.5°C and the reductions needed to bring warming back down. National reporting emphasized different responsibilities.
stories.whyItMatters: The assessment provides a dated benchmark for comparing future emissions, climate policy and temperature projections.
stories.selectionRationale: Long-term international consequences and contrasting national coverage justify following the assessment after its October 21 launch.
stories.evidenceNote: All three articles discuss the same UNEP assessment. They corroborate what the report says, not independent climate measurements. The reference is UNEP’s institutional explanatory news article, not an independent newsroom audit.
